## Schemas

### audio-data.schema.json

**VSift audio data v1** ([the schema](../../../schemas/v1/audio-data.schema.json))

The data member of a complete or partial audio result (P09, ADR 0019): one WAV clip of at most 30 s of the session's audio (16 kHz mono signed 16-bit, decision D5). request is the requested half-open range; a range that runs past the end of the source is clipped to it and range_clipped is true. The single selection has role requested, requested_us the requested start, actual_us the first decoded sample's time and delta_us their difference. items holds the audio_evidence record, files delivers the clip as the absolute path of the committed session artifact, valid while the session exists (decision D2). With reused true the record was committed by an identical earlier request and returned without running a provider or writing anything. Times are integer microseconds on the normalized source timeline.

| Member | Type | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `session_id` | string | yes | pattern `^ses_[a-z0-9]{16,64}$` |
| `source_id` | string | yes | pattern `^src_sha256_[0-9a-f]{64}$` |
| `operation` | constant "audio" | yes |  |
| `request` | object | yes |  |
| `request.from_us` | integer | yes | at least 0 |
| `request.to_us` | integer | yes | at least 1 |
| `request_key` | string | yes | Digest of the session, source, stream selector, operation, canonical request, adapter profile and provider fingerprint. An identical later request with a known fingerprint is answered from the complete record with this key.; pattern `^opk_sha256_[0-9a-f]{64}$` |
| `reused` | boolean | yes | true when the record was committed by an earlier identical request and returned without running a provider or writing anything; every file was verified again. |
| `profile` | constant "p09-r0-v1" | yes |  |
| `tool_fingerprint` | string or null | yes | The media provider's fingerprint (executables' identity, adapter, reviewed policy, host isolation and verifying authority), or null when it could not be computed; then the evidence_id also digests the image and nothing is reused.; pattern `^[0-9a-f]{64}$` |
| `source_check` | "identity" \| "full_hash" | yes | How the call that committed the record checked the session's source copy (decision D1): identity (its on-disk identity matched the one recorded after an earlier full hash) or full_hash. |
| `selections` | array of object | yes | Which item each requested time resolved to. requested_us is the time the role refers to: the requested time (requested, frame_get), the anchor frame's time (before and after), a burst target's time (target) or the parent frame's time (requested, crop). delta_us is actual_us - requested_us.; exactly 1 items |
| `selections[].role` | constant "requested" | no |  |
| `range_clipped` | boolean | yes | true when the requested range ran past the end of the source and the clip covers only its part before the end. |
| `items` | array of object, see [audio-evidence.schema.json](#audio-evidenceschemajson) | yes | exactly 1 items |
| `files` | array of object | yes | One delivered file per item, in item order: the absolute path of the committed session artifact (decision D2). It is valid while the session exists (until it is closed, expires or is cleaned) and must not be written to; retain the session to keep the evidence.; exactly 1 items |
| `files[].media_type` | constant "audio/wav" | no |  |
| `partial_reason` | "frame_budget" \| "pixel_budget" \| "byte_budget" \| "session_evidence_budget" \| "deadline_exceeded" \| "cancelled" or null | yes | Why the call returned fewer items than its request named, or null for a complete result. The items returned are committed evidence. Only complete records are reused. |

### audio-evidence.schema.json

**VSift audio evidence record v1** ([the schema](../../../schemas/v1/audio-evidence.schema.json))

One published audio_evidence record (P09, ADR 0019): a WAV clip of the session's audio, extracted by audio. Its evidence_id digests only what fixes its samples (session, source, audio stream, adapter profile, provider fingerprint and the clipped range), so every request that resolves to the same range names the same record. range is the half-open range the clip was decoded for (the request clipped to the source); actual_start_us is the normalized time of the first decoded sample, which may lie after range.start_us (for example AAC priming or a stream that starts late). The samples are the delivered file named in the result's files, never embedded. Times are integer microseconds on the normalized source timeline.

| `stream_index` | integer | yes | 0 to 4294967295 |
| `range` | object | yes |  |
| `range.start_us` | integer | yes | at least 0 |
| `range.end_us` | integer | yes | at least 1 |
| `actual_start_us` | integer | yes | at least 0 |
| `audio` | object | yes | The delivered clip: WAV, 16 kHz mono signed 16-bit little-endian PCM (decision D5), at most 30 s and 1 MiB, its SHA-256 and size in bytes. |
| `audio.media_type` | constant "audio/wav" | yes |  |
| `audio.sample_rate` | constant 16000 | yes |  |
| `audio.channels` | constant 1 | yes |  |
| `audio.sample_format` | constant "s16le" | yes |  |
| `audio.sha256` | string | yes | pattern `^[0-9a-f]{64}$` |
| `audio.bytes` | integer | yes | 44 to 1048576 |
| `profile` | constant "p09-r0-v1" | yes |  |
| `tool_fingerprint` | string or null | yes | The media provider's fingerprint (executables' identity, adapter, reviewed policy, host isolation and verifying authority), or null when it could not be computed; then the evidence_id also digests the image and nothing is reused.; pattern `^[0-9a-f]{64}$` |

### bundle-evidence-record.schema.json

**VSift retained bundle evidence record v1** ([the schema](../../../schemas/v1/bundle-evidence-record.schema.json))

The content of a session or retained bundle artifact whose kind is evidence_record (P09, ADR 0019): the lineage of one evidence call (frame get, frame neighbours, frame burst, crop or audio), stored as compact UTF-8 JSON and named artifact-<sha256>.json. This is a storage record, not an operation response: schema_version is the integer record version and format names the record. It holds the call's request key and canonical parameters, which item each requested time resolved to with requested and actual time and their signed delta, the items (stream, exact timestamp and time base, crop region or clipped audio range, the digest and size of the frame_png or audio_wav artifact that holds the pixels or samples, the provider fingerprint and how the call checked the source copy) and why the call stopped short, if it did. It never holds an operation identifier, a path or media bytes. Times are integer microseconds on the normalized source timeline. A session holds at most 384 evidence artifacts (images, clips and records together) within 512 artifacts and a record is at most 256 KiB. bundle validate decodes every record strictly (unknown fields, values and newer versions are rejected), re-derives the request key and every item identity, checks that each item's file is in the bundle with the item's kind, size and digest, that an image's PNG header states the item's dimensions and a clip's WAV header 16 kHz mono signed 16-bit PCM, that every crop parent and neighbours anchor is an item of the bundle, and that items with one identity agree on everything but their source check. This schema describes its shape.

| Member | Type | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `schema_version` | constant 1 | yes |  |
| `format` | constant "vsift.evidence_record" | yes |  |
| `request_key` | string | yes | Digest of the session, source, stream selector, operation, canonical parameters, adapter profile and provider fingerprint. A later call with the same key and a known fingerprint is answered from a complete record without running a provider.; pattern `^opk_sha256_[0-9a-f]{64}$` |
| `session_id` | string | yes | pattern `^ses_[a-z0-9]{16,64}$` |
| `source_id` | string | yes | pattern `^src_sha256_[0-9a-f]{64}$` |
| `profile` | constant "p09-r0-v1" | yes |  |
| `tool_fingerprint` | string or null | yes | The media provider's fingerprint (executables' identity, adapter and policy), or null when it could not be computed; then the item identity also digests the media and nothing is reused.; pattern `^[0-9a-f]{64}$` |
| `request` | object or object or object or object or object | yes | The canonical request, named by its operation. |
| `request.frame_get` | object | yes |  |
| `request.frame_get.at_us` | integer | yes | at least 0 |
| `request.frame_get.policy` | "at_or_after" \| "displayed_at" | yes |  |

### bundle-transcript-record.schema.json

**VSift retained bundle transcript record v1** ([the schema](../../../schemas/v1/bundle-transcript-record.schema.json))

The content of a retained bundle artifact whose bundle.json kind is transcript_record: one immutable transcript revision with all of its segments, stored as compact UTF-8 JSON and named artifact-<sha256>.json. This is a storage record, not an operation response: schema_version is the integer record version (1 for an imported revision, 2 for a local-ASR revision) and format names the record. Times are integer microseconds on the normalized source timeline. text is the stored segment text with recognised markup removed (lines joined with \n; no other control character). Text is untrusted input: sanitize it before display. bundle validate decodes every transcript record strictly (unknown fields, values and newer versions are rejected) and re-checks every segment against the rule that produced it; this schema describes its shape.

| Member | Type | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `schema_version` | constant 1 | yes |  |
| `format` | constant "vsift.transcript_record" | yes |  |
| `revision_id` | string | yes | pattern `^trv_[a-z0-9]{16,64}$` |
| `revision` | integer | yes | 1 to 4294967295 |
| `source_id` | string | yes | pattern `^src_sha256_[0-9a-f]{64}$` |
| `source_segment` | object | yes | The one closed source segment of a finite file: index 0 from time 0 to the probed duration. |
| `source_segment.id` | string | yes | pattern `^sgm_[a-z0-9]{16,64}$` |
| `source_segment.index` | constant 0 | yes |  |
| `source_segment.start_us` | constant 0 | yes |  |
| `source_segment.end_us` | integer | yes | at least 1 |
| `source_segment.state` | "closed" | yes |  |
| `origin` | "imported_srt" \| "imported_webvtt" | yes |  |
| `offset_us` | integer | yes | -86400000000 to 86400000000 |
| `sidecar` | object | yes | Identity of the exact supplied bytes that were parsed. |
| `sidecar.sha256` | string | yes | pattern `^[0-9a-f]{64}$` |
| `sidecar.bytes` | integer | yes | 1 to 8388608 |

### bundle-visual-index-record.schema.json

**VSift retained bundle visual-index record v1** ([the schema](../../../schemas/v1/bundle-visual-index-record.schema.json))

The content of a session or retained bundle artifact whose kind is visual_index_record (P08): one immutable revision of the session's visual-candidate index, stored as compact UTF-8 JSON and named artifact-<sha256>.json. This is a storage record, not an operation response: schema_version is the integer record version and format names the record. A revision holds every window of the revision before it unchanged, so only the newest is read; windows that are absent have not been analysed. Times are integer microseconds on the normalized source timeline. The record holds no pixels or sample data, only candidates. A session holds at most 64 such records of at most 8 MiB. bundle validate decodes every record strictly (unknown fields, values and newer versions are rejected) and re-derives what a record could claim without being true: each window's range from its ordinal and duration_us, each candidate's span start from its representative time and its end from the next candidate or the window end, sample counts, every change against the r0-visual-v1 policy, that every 10 s cell holds a candidate or is listed in frameless_cells, and every candidate and revision identity from the session, source, stream, profile, window and time. This schema describes its shape.

| Member | Type | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `schema_version` | constant 1 | yes |  |
| `format` | constant "vsift.visual_index_record" | yes |  |
| `index_id` | string | yes | pattern `^vix_[a-z0-9]{16,64}$` |
| `revision` | integer | yes | 1 to 4294967295 |
| `session_id` | string | yes | pattern `^ses_[a-z0-9]{16,64}$` |
| `source_id` | string | yes | pattern `^src_sha256_[0-9a-f]{64}$` |
| `stream_index` | integer | yes | 0 to 4294967295 |
| `displayed_dimensions` | object | yes |  |
| `displayed_dimensions.width` | integer | yes | 1 to 4294967295 |
| `displayed_dimensions.height` | integer | yes | 1 to 4294967295 |
| `duration_us` | integer | yes | The probed source duration the 60 s window grid is cut from; at most four hours.; 1 to 14400000000 |
| `profile` | constant "r0-visual-v1" | yes |  |
| `windows` | array of object or object | yes | Analysed and undecodable windows in strictly ascending ordinal order.; at most 240 items |
| `windows[].ordinal` | integer | yes | 0 to 239 |
| `windows[].start_us` | integer | yes | at least 0 |
| `windows[].end_us` | integer | yes | at least 1 |
| `windows[].state` | constant "analysed" | yes |  |
| `windows[].sample_count` | integer | yes | Decoded samples inside the window (the lead-in sample is not counted).; 0 to 122 |
| `windows[].dropped_candidates` | integer | yes | Change candidates the 32-candidate budget dropped.; 0 to 122 |
| `windows[].frameless_cells` | array of object | yes | 10 s cells of the window in which no frame was decoded.; at most 6 items |
| `windows[].frameless_cells[].start_us` | integer | yes | at least 0 |
| `windows[].frameless_cells[].end_us` | integer | yes | at least 1 |
| `windows[].candidates` | array of object | yes | at most 32 items |
| `windows[].candidates[].id` | string | yes | pattern `^vcd_[a-z0-9]{16,64}$` |
| `windows[].candidates[].reason` | "first_frame" \| "visual_change" \| "motion_start" \| "settled_after_motion" \| "periodic_coverage" | yes |  |
| `windows[].candidates[].representative_us` | integer | yes | at least 0 |
| `windows[].candidates[].span_end_us` | integer | yes | at least 1 |
| `windows[].candidates[].sample_count` | integer | yes | 1 to 122 |
| `windows[].candidates[].stability` | "settled" \| "transient" \| "in_motion" \| "open_at_window_end" | yes |  |
| `windows[].candidates[].visual_hash` | string | yes | pattern `^[0-9a-f]{16}$` |
| `windows[].candidates[].change` | object or null | yes |  |
| `windows[].candidates[].change.previous_sample_us` | integer | yes | at least 0 |
| `windows[].candidates[].change.changed_blocks` | integer | yes | 0 to 144 |
| `windows[].candidates[].change.max_block_delta` | integer | yes | 0 to 255 |
| `windows[].ordinal` | integer | yes | 0 to 239 |

| `windows[].end_us` | integer | yes | at least 1 |

### candidates-data.schema.json

**VSift candidates data v1** ([the schema](../../../schemas/v1/candidates-data.schema.json))

The data member of a complete or partial candidates result (P08): one bounded page of the visual candidates whose representative time lies in the requested range, in time order, as published visual-candidate evidence records. A call first analyses the range's missing 60 s windows, at most 30 (30 minutes of media) per call; index names the revision the page was read from and its fixed sampling grid. coverage says which parts of the range (clipped to the video) are analysed and lists every typed gap. Validate the envelope with operation-response.schema.json: its coverage member is truncated, and its status partial, exactly when coverage.gaps is not empty. Pass next_cursor back with the same session and range to continue; it never analyses anything, and it is rejected for any other session or range, after the session expires, or once a later call has analysed a window of its range.

| Member | Type | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `session_id` | string | yes | pattern `^ses_[a-z0-9]{16,64}$` |
| `range` | object | yes | The requested half-open range. |
| `range.from_us` | integer | yes | at least 0 |
| `range.to_us` | integer | yes | at least 1 |
| `index` | object | yes | The committed visual-index revision the page was read from. Each call that analyses anything commits a new revision holding every window of the one before it unchanged, so candidate identities never change. |
| `index.index_id` | string | yes | pattern `^vix_[a-z0-9]{16,64}$` |
| `index.number` | integer | yes | 1 to 64 |
| `index.profile` | constant "r0-visual-v1" | yes |  |
| `index.duration_us` | integer | yes | The video's probed duration; windows and coverage are clipped to it.; at least 1 |
| `index.window_us` | constant 60000000 | yes |  |
| `index.sample_interval_us` | constant 500000 | yes | Decoded frames are sampled at least this far apart (2 Hz). |
| `index.coverage_interval_us` | constant 10000000 | yes | Every cell of this length that holds a decoded frame has at least one candidate. |
| `coverage` | object | yes |  |
| `coverage.searched_range` | object | yes | The requested range clipped to the video. |
| `coverage.searched_range.from_us` | integer | yes | at least 0 |
| `coverage.searched_range.to_us` | integer | yes | at least 1 |
| `coverage.analyzed` | array of object | yes | Parts of searched_range that analysed windows cover, merged and in start order. no_decoded_frame and candidate_budget_exhausted gaps lie inside them.; at most 100 items |
| `coverage.analyzed[].from_us` | integer | yes | at least 0 |
| `coverage.analyzed[].to_us` | integer | yes | at least 1 |
| `coverage.gaps` | array of object | yes | Every typed gap of searched_range in start order; touching gaps of one reason are merged, except budget gaps, which stay per window.; at most 100 items |
| `coverage.gaps[].from_us` | integer | yes | at least 0 |
| `coverage.gaps[].to_us` | integer | yes | at least 1 |
| `coverage.gaps[].reason` | "not_analyzed" \| "deadline_exceeded" \| "undecodable" \| "no_decoded_frame" \| "candidate_budget_exhausted" | yes | not_analyzed: not analysed yet; call candidates again for the range. deadline_exceeded: the window's decode timed out in this call; a later call retries it. undecodable: the media tools could not decode the window (recorded, not retried). no_decoded_frame: a 10 s cell of an analysed window without a decoded frame. candidate_budget_exhausted: the window changed more often than its 32-candidate budget; dropped_candidates says how many change candidates were dropped. |
| `coverage.gaps[].dropped_candidates` | integer | yes | Change candidates dropped by the window's budget; 0 for every other reason.; 0 to 65535 |
| `coverage.ranges_truncated` | boolean | yes | True when analyzed or gaps held more than 100 entries and only the first 100 are listed. |
| `items` | array of object, see [visual-candidate.schema.json](#visual-candidateschemajson) | yes | at most 100 items |
| `next_cursor` | string or null | yes | 1 to 512 characters |

### evidence-event.schema.json

**VSift JSONL evidence record event v1** ([the schema](../../../schemas/v1/evidence-event.schema.json))

One evidence record in an --events jsonl stream. Evidence events precede the single terminal event (terminal-event.schema.json) that ends the stream; sequence numbers start at 0 and are contiguous across every event of the stream. record_type names the schema of record. key is the record's upsert key: evidence records are immutable, so the same (record_type, key) always carries the same record and a consumer may upsert by it idempotently.

| Member | Type | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `schema_version` | constant "1" | yes |  |
| `event` | constant "evidence" | yes |  |
| `sequence` | integer | yes | at least 0 |
| `command` | string | yes | at most 64 characters; pattern `^[a-z]+(?:-[a-z]+)*(?:[.][a-z]+(?:-[a-z]+)*)?$` |
| `operation_id` | string or null | yes | pattern `^op_[a-z0-9]{16,64}$` |
| `record_type` | "transcript_segment" \| "visual_candidate" \| "frame_evidence" \| "audio_evidence" | yes |  |
| `key` | string | yes | at most 128 characters; pattern `^[a-z]+_[a-z0-9_]+$` |
| `record` | object | yes |  |

This schema also holds 4 conditional rules (a member that is required, or fixed, when another has a given value); read [the schema](../../../schemas/v1/evidence-event.schema.json) for them.

### frame-data.schema.json

**VSift frame and crop data v1** ([the schema](../../../schemas/v1/frame-data.schema.json))

The data member of a complete or partial frame.get, frame.neighbours, frame.burst or crop result (P09, ADR 0019). operation names the call and fixes the shape of request, neighbours and burst. The result presents the lineage record the call committed, or, with reused true, the complete record an identical earlier request committed (no provider ran and nothing was written). selections say which item each requested time resolved to, with requested and actual time and their signed delta; items are the distinct frame_evidence records in the record's order; files deliver each item's image as the absolute path of the committed session artifact, valid while the session exists and never to be written to (decision D2). A result whose call stopped on a budget, the deadline or a cancellation after extracting something has partial_reason set and envelope status partial. Times are integer microseconds on the normalized source timeline.

| Member | Type | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `session_id` | string | yes | pattern `^ses_[a-z0-9]{16,64}$` |
| `source_id` | string | yes | pattern `^src_sha256_[0-9a-f]{64}$` |
| `operation` | "frame_get" \| "frame_neighbours" \| "frame_burst" \| "crop" | yes |  |
| `request` | object | yes |  |
| `request_key` | string | yes | Digest of the session, source, stream selector, operation, canonical request, adapter profile and provider fingerprint. An identical later request with a known fingerprint is answered from the complete record with this key.; pattern `^opk_sha256_[0-9a-f]{64}$` |

### frame-evidence.schema.json

**VSift frame evidence record v1** ([the schema](../../../schemas/v1/frame-evidence.schema.json))

One published frame_evidence record (P09, ADR 0019): a whole displayed frame of the session's video, or a rectangle of one, extracted by frame get, frame neighbours, frame burst or crop. Its evidence_id digests only what fixes its pixels (session, source, stream, adapter profile, provider fingerprint, the frame's exact timestamp and time base, and a crop's region), so every request that resolves to the same frame names the same record; request-specific facts (requested time, policy, delta, candidate) are in the result's request and selections. The pixels are the delivered file named in the result's files, never embedded. Times are integer microseconds on the normalized source timeline.

### handoff-check-data.schema.json

**VSift handoff.check data v1** ([the schema](../../../schemas/v1/handoff-check-data.schema.json))

The data member of a complete handoff.check result (P13 PR 5, issue #213, ADR 0023 decisions G and H): whether an agent's draft report passed the skill's handoff checks. The command reads the whole report (at most 64 KiB of UTF-8 from standard input or --file), finds its one vsift-handoff block, reads closed values written in another letter case as the schema's spelling (case_notes), validates the JSON against the skill-owned handoff.schema.json and the handoff rules, and checks the whole report's text for local paths, links and raw hidden or control characters. With --session it also resolves every cited identity against that session's committed records, read-only; a closed, expired or unknown session is a gap in session, not a failure. valid is true exactly when errors is empty; the command exits 0 whenever it read the draft. No finding repeats text from the draft: pointer is an RFC 6901 pointer built from the handoff schema's own member names and array indices (an unknown member is reported at its object, with the allowed members), line is a 1-based line of the report, rule is closed, allowed lists the schema's own values where the rule has them, and message is fixed prose. Each list holds at most 100 findings; truncated says more were found.

### job-batch-data.schema.json

**VSift job.batch data v1** ([the schema](../../../schemas/v1/job-batch-data.schema.json))

The data member of the terminal job.batch result (P11, ADR 0021): per-status counts, one item per line processed (at most 1,000; blank lines have none), the first line not started (after a shutdown, a line limit or an input error; null when every line was read) and why the batch stopped. Every request's full result was streamed before it as a result event (result-event.schema.json). The batch's exit status follows maintainer decision D5: 0 when every item is complete or partial, 6 when a shutdown stopped the batch, else the most severe failure class in the order 7 > 1 > 5 > 3 > 2 > 4.

### job-data.schema.json

**VSift job data v1** ([the schema](../../../schemas/v1/job-data.schema.json))

The data member of a complete job.status or job.cancel result: one recoverable job (P10, ADR 0020). Validate the envelope with operation-response.schema.json. state is what a reader observes: a job whose process ended without recording it is reported interrupted (or succeeded, when its commit is in the session's manifest chain), never running. live_owner says a process holds the job right now. resumable says whether job resume would run it now, and resumable_reason why (interrupted, not_started) or why not (live_owner, succeeded, failed, cancelled, session_not_open). operation_id is the id a retry should carry: the first one a caller bound with --operation-id, or for a succeeded job the one its commit is recorded under. request.range is the range the caller asked for (null for the whole source). progress.chunks_total is how many chunks the recognised range is cut into (null for a job created before P10 PR 3) and chunks_checkpointed how many chunk checkpoints the job keeps now (a succeeded, failed or cancelled job keeps none). attempts counts attempts in the job's current epoch. result names the revision and generation a succeeded job committed; failure the public code that ended the last attempt of an interrupted or failed job. A job never names a path, transcript text or provider output.

| `live_owner` | boolean | yes |  |
| `resumable` | boolean | yes |  |
| `resumable_reason` | "interrupted" \| "not_started" \| "live_owner" \| "succeeded" \| "failed" \| "cancelled" \| "session_not_open" | yes |  |
| `operation_id` | string or null | yes | pattern `^op_[a-z0-9]{16,64}$` |
| `request` | object | yes |  |
| `request.range` | object or null | yes |  |
| `request.range.from_us` | integer | yes | at least 0 |
| `request.range.to_us` | integer | yes | at least 1 |
| `progress` | object | yes |  |
| `progress.chunks_total` | integer or null | yes | 1 to 1024 |
| `progress.chunks_checkpointed` | integer | yes | 0 to 1024 |
| `attempts` | integer | yes | 0 to 16 |
| `result` | object or null | yes |  |
| `result.revision_id` | string | yes | pattern `^trv_[a-z0-9]{16,64}$` |

### job-request.schema.json

**VSift worker job request v1** ([the schema](../../../schemas/v1/job-request.schema.json))

One request of `job run --request <file>`, or one line of `job batch --requests <file>` (P11, ADR 0021). Strict: every member is required except deadline_ms, unknown members are refused, and a document is at most 64 KiB and 16 levels deep. Paths are relative to the operator's --input-root with / between names; besides this pattern the decoder also refuses . and .. names, names ending in a dot or space and Windows device names (CON, NUL, COM1, ...). Steps run in order after the target: retain at most once and followed only by close; close at most once and last; a session target needs at least one step. **VSift worker job result v1** ([the schema](../../../schemas/v1/job-result.schema.json))

### progress-event.schema.json

**VSift JSONL progress event v1** ([the schema](../../../schemas/v1/progress-event.schema.json))

How far a long operation has come, in an --events jsonl stream (P11, ADR 0021): transcript.retranscribe and job.resume (chunks recognised, reused chunks included) the worker commands job.run and job.batch, and setup.install (fetching_artifact: bytes of the artifact being downloaded or imported; installing_components: components of the accepted plan finished). Advisory: at most one per second and 4,096 per request; an update inside the second replaces the pending one, and a host drops progress rather than block on a slow reader, counting the drops in progress_dropped (for this request, before this event). The terminal event stays authoritative. operation_id is null (the command's operation id is in the terminal event); request_operation_id names the worker request, null for other commands; job_id names the recoverable job, when the work runs as one. Every line is at most 64 KiB.

The data member of a complete or partial search result: one bounded page of the transcript segments that match a literal query, in rank order (phrase matches first, then all-terms matches, each by segment start). items are the matching segments as published transcript evidence records (transcript-segment.schema.json), exactly as transcript.get returns them; hits names each item's segment_id and how it matched, in the same order. query.terms is how the query was normalised. range is the requested range, or null when the whole transcript was searched. transcript_coverage says which parts of the searched range a transcript covers: a word said in an untranscribed range cannot be found, and on-screen text is never searched. ### setup-install.schema.json

**VSift setup install data v1** ([the schema](../../../schemas/v1/setup-install.schema.json))

The data of a setup.install result (P13, ADR 0023): every component of the accepted plan, in plan order (ffmpeg_ffprobe, whisper_cli, whisper_model), with what the transaction did to it. A successful result carries it as data; a failed or cancelled one carries the same object as data beside its error, whose code is the first failed component's failure_code. Each component activates atomically on its own: activated and already_current components are installed and selected; a rerun of the same accepted plan continues from the first component not yet current. A failed component names the step that stopped it and a typed reason; blocked means an earlier component stopped the transaction first. stage says what cleanup did with the component's private stage (retained only when its ownership or content could not be proved). Every string is a closed identifier or a reviewed version; no path, URL, server text or credential.

| `components[].component` | "ffmpeg_ffprobe" \| "whisper_cli" \| "whisper_model" | yes |  |
| `components[].version` | string | yes | pattern `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9._-]{0,63}$` |
| `components[].status` | "activated" \| "already_current" \| "failed" | yes |  |
| `components[].step` | "download" \| "import" \| "stage" \| "smoke" \| "activate" or null | yes |  |
| `components[].reason` | "tls" \| "redirect_policy" \| "http_status" \| "proxy_auth" \| "offline" \| "size" \| "artifact_missing" \| "artifact_not_regular_file" \| "digest_mismatch" \| "size_mismatch" \| "review_mismatch" \| "storage" \| "missing_executable" \| "wrong_architecture" \| "not_executable" \| "banner_mismatch" \| "output_over_bound" \| "deadline_exceeded" \| "unexpected_extra_file" \| "changed_content" \| "provider_failed" \| "fixture_mismatch" \| "preparation" \| "invalid_request" \| "cancelled" \| "blocked" or null | yes |  |
| `components[].failure_code` | "DOWNLOAD_FAILED" \| "INVALID_ARGUMENT" \| "INTEGRITY_FAILURE" \| "STORAGE_IO" \| "MISSING_CAPABILITY" \| "CANCELLED" or null | yes |  |
| `components[].smoke_check` | "layout" \| "banner" \| "media_fixture" \| "speech_fixture" \| "recheck" or null | yes |  |
| `components[].missing_shared_library` | string | no | Present only when a reviewed program could not start because the loader could not find a shared library: its plain file name (for example libgomp.so.1), read from the program's own error output and validated; the reason is still provider_failed. ### setup-list.schema.json

**VSift setup list data v1** ([the schema](../../../schemas/v1/setup-list.schema.json))

The data of a setup.list result (P13 PR 6, ADR 0023): every managed component, always in the order ffmpeg_ffprobe, whisper_cli, whisper_model, with its selection, its selected and previous versions and every published version with whether it verifies. Read-only: listing creates and changes nothing. managed_install says whether managed installation can install on this host (catalogue_accepted only on Ubuntu 24.04 x86-64); managed_folder is absent when this user has no managed folder, and every component then has no versions. selection is verified when commands use the selected version (it verifies and its manifest is the one the selection names), unverified when they do not (the version is missing, does not verify or is being removed), unreadable when the selection cannot be read, and none when nothing is selected. A version's state is verified, removal_interrupted (a removal stopped; setup remove finishes it) or unverified with a fault. stale_stages and retained_stages count stages abandoned by earlier installations that setup remove --stale-stages would remove or would keep for the user. Every string is a closed identifier, a managed version key or fixed prose; no path.

### setup-plan.schema.json

**VSift reviewed setup plan v1** ([the schema](../../../schemas/v1/setup-plan.schema.json))

A read-only setup plan. Its intent (profile, target, managed_install, catalogue, plan_digest, every action's reviewed artifact, each dependency's and the model's disposition and next step) is what plan_digest binds and what setup install compares with a saved plan. Its observed state (readiness, install_needed, each dependency's and the model's status, each action's state) is what commands would use now, managed versions included (P13 PR 4): it changes as setup install applies the plan and is not compared, so a rerun of the same accepted setup install continues. An action whose state is current is installed at the plan's version; install_needed is false when every action is current or there is none.

### setup-remove.schema.json

**VSift setup remove data v1** ([the schema](../../../schemas/v1/setup-remove.schema.json))

The data of a setup.remove result (P13 PR 6, ADR 0023), successful or failed. target is version (setup remove <component> --version <version>: one unselected version), component (setup remove <component>: its selection first, then every version) or stale_stages (setup remove --stale-stages: stages abandoned by interrupted or failed installations, and half-written selection pointers). Each version handled is listed with its status: removed, already_absent, in_use (a running job holds it; it is kept and a later setup remove removes it), selected, unexpected_content (an invalid manifest, a link, a folder or an unknown name: kept for the user) or storage_failure. Only positively identified content inside the private managed folder is ever removed; nothing is followed through a link. When anything asked for remains, the result is a failure (BUSY for a version in use, STORAGE_IO for kept content) with this same object as data beside the error. No path.

### setup-repair.schema.json

**VSift setup repair data v1** ([the schema](../../../schemas/v1/setup-repair.schema.json))

The data of a complete setup.repair result (P13 PR 6; ADR 0007 and ADR 0023: repair is read-only, it diagnoses and emits a plan). Repair changes, creates, selects and downloads nothing, and a store that needs repair is still a complete result: status is nothing_installed (no managed folder), healthy or needs_repair. Each finding says what is wrong (kind, the component and version concerned, a count for stages, pointers and entries, the fault of an unverified version), fix names how, summary is fixed prose, and command is the existing vsift command that applies the fix (an executable and argument array of fixed words and managed keys, run without a shell), or null for fix manual: content VSift cannot prove its own, which the user deletes. The findings are in the order to apply them. A reinstall is always a new setup plan accepted with setup install. No path.

| `findings` | array of object | yes | at most 4096 items |

| `findings[].fix` | "rollback" \| "rollback_to_version" \| "remove_version" \| "remove_component_and_reinstall" \| "remove_stale_stages" \| "manual" | yes |  |
| `findings[].summary` | string | yes | 1 to 1024 characters |

### setup-rollback.schema.json

**VSift setup rollback data v1** ([the schema](../../../schemas/v1/setup-rollback.schema.json))

The data of a complete setup.rollback result (P13 PR 6, ADR 0023). Without --version the component returns to the version its selection records as selected before; with --version it selects that installed version. Either way the version is selected only after it verifies (its manifest exists and every file matches it; a return to the recorded previous version also requires the manifest recorded), in one atomic rename, and the version it replaced becomes the new previous one, so a second rollback returns. status is rolled_back, or already_selected when the named version was already the verified selection and nothing changed. A refusal (nothing installed, no such or earlier version, a version that does not verify, another command holding the managed folder) is a failure result and changes nothing. No path.

| `next_step` | string | yes | 1 to 512 characters |

### terminal-event.schema.json

**VSift JSONL terminal event v1** ([the schema](../../../schemas/v1/terminal-event.schema.json))

The last line of every --events jsonl stream; exactly one per stream. Its sequence is the number of events before it (0 when it is the only line, as for a failure before any other event; since P11 a failure after progress events follows them). A job.batch stream ends with job-batch-data.schema.json data after its lifecycle, progress and result events. Validate result with operation-response.schema.json and result.data with the command's data schema; a transcript.get stream ends with transcript-get-stream-data.schema.json data, and a search stream with search-stream-data.schema.json data, after its evidence events (evidence-event.schema.json).

### transcript-retranscribe-data.schema.json

**VSift transcript.retranscribe data v1** ([the schema](../../../schemas/v1/transcript-retranscribe-data.schema.json))

The data member of a complete transcript.retranscribe result: the new local-ASR revision, committed and now the session's newest. Validate the envelope with operation-response.schema.json. requested_range is the range the caller asked for (null for the whole source); the revision's replaced_range is that range widened to whole segments of the superseded revision. recognised_segment_count is how many of the revision's segments this run recognised; the rest were carried from earlier revisions. The segments themselves are read with transcript get --revision <revision.revision_id>, as a page or an evidence stream. job describes the recoverable job behind the result (P10, ADR 0020): job_id derives from the session and the request's operation key, so rerunning the same request finds the same job; resumed says an interrupted run of it was continued, chunks_reused how many chunks came from its private checkpoints, and replayed that the revision is an earlier commit returned again for a retry with the same operation id, without a new generation. Resume information is never written into the revision, which is the same as an uninterrupted run's.

| Member | Type | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `session_id` | string | yes | pattern `^ses_[a-z0-9]{16,64}$` |
| `requested_range` | object or null | yes |  |
| `requested_range.from_us` | integer | yes | at least 0 |
| `requested_range.to_us` | integer | yes | at least 1 |
| `revision` | object, see [transcript-revision.schema.json](#transcript-revisionschemajson) | yes |  |
| `revision.alignment` | object | no |  |
| `revision.alignment.origin` | constant "local_asr" | no |  |
| `recognised_segment_count` | integer | yes | 0 to 20000 |
| `job` | object | yes |  |
| `job.job_id` | string | yes | pattern `^job_[a-z0-9]{16,64}$` |
| `job.resumed` | boolean | yes |  |
| `job.chunks_reused` | integer | yes | 0 to 1024 |
| `job.replayed` | boolean | yes |  |

### transcript-revision.schema.json

**VSift transcript revision summary v1** ([the schema](../../../schemas/v1/transcript-revision.schema.json))

Identity, alignment and outcome of one immutable transcript revision. Warnings are typed; a warning with excluded_cues true means those cues (or recognised segments) are not in the revision and cannot be cited. An imported revision (alignment origin imported_srt or imported_webvtt) has its offset and sidecar and none of the local-ASR members. A local-ASR revision (origin local_asr) has sidecar null and adds local_asr (what ran, how, over which range and with what chunk outcomes), supersedes and replaced_range (the revision it replaced and the range it replaced there, or null) and carried_segment_count (segments carried unchanged from earlier revisions). For local-ASR warnings, first_cue is the 1-based ordinal of the first affected chunk.

| `alignment.origin` | constant "local_asr" | yes |  |
| `sidecar` | object or null | yes | Identity of the exact supplied bytes that were parsed; null for a local-ASR revision. |

### transcript-segment.schema.json

**VSift transcript segment evidence record v1** ([the schema](../../../schemas/v1/transcript-segment.schema.json))

One citable, timestamped transcript segment. Each record names its own revision, source and source segment so it can be stored or indexed on its own. Times are integer microseconds on the normalized source timeline, half-open [start_us, end_us) with end_us > start_us. Text is untrusted and has been sanitized: lines are joined with \n and no other control character remains. A segment was either imported from a supplied SubRip or WebVTT cue (alignment origin imported_srt or imported_webvtt, with its offset, cue timing and cue location) or recognised locally from the source's audio (origin local_asr, with its chunk, the provider's chunk-relative times and the recognizer; cue is null). A segment carried unchanged into a revision spliced from an earlier one (transcript retranscribe with a range) keeps the alignment and language of the revision that first produced it and names that revision and segment in carried_from; it has its own segment_id in the new revision.

| --- | --- | --- | --- |

| `source_id` | string | yes | pattern `^src_sha256_[0-9a-f]{64}$` |
| `source_segment_id` | string | yes | pattern `^sgm_[a-z0-9]{16,64}$` |
| `start_us` | integer | yes | at least 0 |
| `end_us` | integer | yes | at least 1 |

| `display_text` | string | yes | text with every hidden character written as visible <U+XXXX> notation (U+, uppercase hexadecimal of at least four digits, angle brackets): Unicode 16.0 general category Cf, Default_Ignorable_Code_Point, and U+2028/U+2029. Everything else, including \n and text that literally reads <U+202E>, is exactly as in text, so it equals text when nothing is hidden. The form to quote in a report. Added to v1 on 2026-09-29 (additive; always present).; 1 to 16384 characters |
| `original_text` | string or null | yes | The cue payload as supplied, present only when markup removal changed it. Hidden characters are kept raw.; 1 to 4096 characters |
| `markup` | "none" \| "removed" | yes |  |

### visual-candidate.schema.json

**VSift visual candidate v1** ([the schema](../../../schemas/v1/visual-candidate.schema.json))

One visual candidate, a published evidence record (P08, ADR 0018): a moment at which the selected video stream's screen changed, or a periodic sample of a screen that did not, proposed so an agent need not look at every frame. Each record names its own source, source segment and stream so it can be stored or indexed on its own. Times are integer microseconds on the normalized source timeline. representative_us is the presentation time of the actual decoded frame that represents the candidate (never an interpolated request time); P09 frame get extracts it. span is the half-open time the candidate stands for, from representative_us to the next candidate of its window or the window end. A candidate is never merged across its fixed 60 s window, and a screen that reappears later is a separate candidate with the same visual_hash. Candidates are evidence assistance, not evidence: the original frames are authoritative.

| Member | Type | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `candidate_id` | string | yes | Derived from the session, source, stream, analysis profile, window and representative time, so it never changes when later windows are analysed.; pattern `^vcd_[a-z0-9]{16,64}$` |
| `source_id` | string | yes | pattern `^src_sha256_[0-9a-f]{64}$` |
| `source_segment_id` | string | yes | pattern `^sgm_[a-z0-9]{16,64}$` |
| `stream_index` | integer | yes | Original index of the video stream that was sampled: the first video stream whose codec the media tools decode.; 0 to 4294967295 |
| `window` | object | yes | The fixed 60 s analysis window the candidate belongs to: [60 * ordinal s, min(60 * (ordinal + 1) s, duration)). |
| `window.ordinal` | integer | yes | 0 to 4294967295 |
| `window.from_us` | integer | yes | at least 0 |
| `window.to_us` | integer | yes | at least 1 |
| `representative_us` | integer | yes | at least 0 |
| `span` | object | yes |  |
| `span.from_us` | integer | yes | at least 0 |
| `span.to_us` | integer | yes | at least 1 |
| `change_window` | object or null | yes | Where the change that opened the candidate happened: after from_us (the previous sample) and at or before to_us (representative_us). Null for a first frame or periodic coverage, which no observed change opened. |
| `change_window.from_us` | integer | yes | at least 0 |
| `change_window.to_us` | integer | yes | at least 1 |
| `reasons` | array of "first_frame" \| "visual_change" \| "motion_start" \| "settled_after_motion" \| "periodic_coverage" | yes | Why the candidate was proposed. first_frame: the window's first decoded frame with no earlier sample. visual_change: the screen differs from the state before it. motion_start: the first of three or more consecutive changing samples. settled_after_motion: the first still sample after motion. periodic_coverage: no change fell in its 10 s cell (or the window continues the screen before it), so its first sample represents it.; 1 to 5 items; items are unique |
| `stability` | "settled" \| "transient" \| "in_motion" \| "open_at_window_end" | yes | settled: the screen held for at least two consecutive samples. transient: seen in exactly one sample, then it changed. in_motion: changing from sample to sample. open_at_window_end: seen only in the window's last sample, so whether it held is unknown. |
| `change` | object or null | yes | The size of the change that opened the candidate, null when change_window is null. Both values are uncalibrated integers of the r0-visual-v1 grey 16x9 block grid (changed_blocks 0..144 blocks whose mean moved by at least 4 levels; max_block_delta 0..255 levels). They order changes by size; they are not a confidence or a probability. |
| `change.changed_blocks` | integer | yes | 0 to 144 |
| `change.max_block_delta` | integer | yes | 0 to 255 |
| `visual_hash` | string | yes | A 64-bit difference hash of the representative frame as 16 lowercase hexadecimal digits: a similarity key that shows when a screen repeats, not a security digest.; pattern `^[0-9a-f]{16}$` |
| `sample_count` | integer | yes | Decoded samples inside span.; 1 to 122 |
| `displayed_dimensions` | object | yes | The sampled stream's orientation-correct displayed size in pixels; what the representative frame shows. |
| `displayed_dimensions.width` | integer | yes | at least 1 |
| `displayed_dimensions.height` | integer | yes | at least 1 |
| `analysis` | object | yes | How the candidate was found: the analysis profile and the size of the grey samples it compared (no image is kept). |
| `analysis.profile` | constant "r0-visual-v1" | yes |  |
| `analysis.width` | constant 128 | yes |  |
| `analysis.height` | constant 72 | yes |  |

### workspace-data.schema.json

**VSift session.init-workspace data v1** ([the schema](../../../schemas/v1/workspace-data.schema.json))

The data member of a complete session.init-workspace result (P11, ADR 0021, maintainer decisions D1 and D2): the policy of an explicitly initialised worker workspace, immutable once created. durability durable is accepted only where OS-crash durability is qualified (publication os_crash_durable); a session of the workspace lives session_retention_seconds (default 604800, one hour to 2592000) and may be renewed within it. outcome is created, or already_initialized when the workspace existed with exactly this policy. It never names the workspace's path.

| `profile` | constant "durable_workspace" | yes |  |
| `durability` | "durable" \| "ephemeral" | yes |  |
| `publication` | "process_crash_consistent" \| "os_crash_durable" | yes |  |
| `admission_capacity` | integer | yes | 1 to 64 |
| `session_retention_seconds` | integer | yes | 3600 to 2592000 |
| `outcome` | "created" \| "already_initialized" | yes |  |

This schema also holds 1 conditional rule (a member that is required, or fixed, when another has a given value); read [the schema](../../../schemas/v1/workspace-data.schema.json) for it.
